intro.text: A quiet parshman assigned to Kaladin's Bridge Four, whom the crew calls Shen.
A parshman in Bridge Four, known to the crew as Shen, who serves with them in Dalinar Kholin's warcamp.
A listener who spied on the Alethi warcamps disguised as a parshman, and a loyal member of Bridge Four.
A listener and member of Bridge Four, bonded to the mistspren Tumi as a Truthwatcher.

items.text: Rlain grew up in a hollow stone building overgrown with crem. His parents died in a flood when he was seven, and he took to raising axehounds, a loner who got on better with his hounds than with people.

Rlain and his friend Thude were among the first listeners to take warform. Given his people's best spy training, he slipped into the Alethi warcamps in dullform, posing as a parshman slave, and spent about three years moving between owners, the last a quartermaster's overseer in Sadeas's camp.

Hashal put Rlain in Bridge Four to test whether parshmen could run bridges. It was a cruel posting: his own people had orders to shoot at parshman bridgemen, and from afar they could not tell him apart. He never broke cover.

Bridge Four was secretly training with spears, and Teft worried the parshman would betray them. Kaladin would not arm Shen either, so he joined Rock, Lopen and Dabbid scavenging the chasms with Syl's help while the others trained.

Shen ran bridges and chasm duty without trouble. When Kaladin began looting a Parshendi corpse, Shen tried to stop him and Teft and Moash held him in a chokehold. Freed on Kaladin's order, he stood guard over the body, as he had done before.

Seeing how much the dead mattered to Shen gave Kaladin the idea of wearing Parshendi carapace to draw enemy fire. When Kaladin did so, Shen wept and could not look at him, and Matal let him stay behind on the runs that followed, including the Battle of the Tower.

Freed with the other bridgemen, Shen moved to Dalinar's warcamp. When the tattooist refused to mark him, calling him property, Teft led the crew in defending him as a free man. Afterwards he grew more at ease, even asking Rock for second helpings.
Still unwilling to arm a parshman, Kaladin set Shen and Dabbid to help Lopen and Rock with supplies and cooking for the bridgemen-turned-soldiers.
Risking his cover, Shen asked Kaladin why he had no spear like the others, and whether he was simply Bridge Four's slave. Shaken, Kaladin still said no, fearing the lighteyes would not stand for it.
After some weeks, Kaladin asked Dalinar for leave to arm Shen and put him on guard duty. Holding the spear with reverence, Shen told Kaladin he was a good man, but fell silent when Moash arrived.

On guard duty with Adolin, Rlain heard that Eshonai, his former commander, had changed into stormform. That night he left the warcamps to warn his people, telling Kaladin he was going and thanking him for his teaching.

At Narak Rlain found an army of stormform listeners and realised the people he knew were lost. He took warform again and returned to the Alethi armies just before the battle, causing a tense standoff.
Questioned by Dalinar, Rlain admitted to spying, warned of stormform and the return of the listeners' ancient gods, and agreed to guide the army to Narak quickly for the sake of any listeners left.

He helped Shallan map a route across the plateaus. When the stormforms began singing, he urged Dalinar to stop the song at any cost. Kept under guard during the fighting, he advised Dalinar throughout, and Dalinar pardoned him.

Rlain moved into Urithiru with Bridge Four, but the gulf remained. Kholin soldiers eyed him with suspicion, and bridgemen often overlooked him or showed thoughtless prejudice even when trying to include him.
Believing himself the last of his people, he carried heavy grief. After a hard day Kaladin drew him into talking about it, and Rlain resolved to let Bridge Four help share the weight.
As Bridge Four became Windrunners, Rlain found other ways to help, aiding Navani's research and leading her push to speed crop growth with the listeners' method of Stormlight and rhythmic drumming.

Many in the tower still treated him as a tamed savage or a noble relic of a lost people. He tried workform to look less like the enemy, but people then treated him as a parshman, so he went back to warform.
Kaladin found him an honorspren, but Rlain learned Yunfah had been pressed into it and refused, choosing to wait for a spren who wanted him. He stayed in Urithiru when Bridge Four left for Emul.

When Odium's forces seized the tower, Rlain helped Kaladin carry the stricken Teft to safety. Seeing a long occupation ahead, he chose to hide among the invaders and use his spycraft to help from inside.
Painting his tattoo into his pattern, he moved freely and stole the only full set of tower maps, but within a day a routine check exposed him and he was imprisoned.
Venli, who had thought him long dead, visited him in prison. She told him Odium had wiped out the other surviving listeners, and showed no wish to side with the humans.

Venli had him released into her care as her last kin and set him to tend the fallen Radiants with Lirin and Hesina. He grew close to Kaladin's family and studied the stolen maps with Venli and Hesina.
Dabbid came seeking help for a dying Kaladin. Rlain helped Venli free Lift, then guided Dabbid up the tower to Kaladin, talking their way past the patrols.
Venli confessed that thousands of listeners had survived and told him the truth of her part in events. Horrified, he warned her not to seek them out and play into Raboniel's hands.
As fighting broke out in the tower, Rlain and Dabbid set up triage for the wounded. Finding Teft's body, Rlain mourned him with the listeners' Song of the Fallen.
Surrounded by Fused while leading humans to safety, Rlain prepared to fight. The mistspren Tumi, who had been watching him, named him Bridger of Minds and bonded him, making him a Truthwatcher.

appearance.text: Shen looks like any parshman: a round, hairless face and a stout, thick body, a little taller than most parshmen but still short for an Alethi.
In warform he is as tall as an Alethi and more muscular, with an orange-red skullplate and carapace armour on his chest, thighs and arms.
His skin is marbled red and black in a distinctive pattern, and he bears the Bridge Four freedom tattoo on his forehead.

personality.text: Quiet and careful, he slowly grows bolder with Bridge Four, asking Rock for seconds and pressing Kaladin about why he alone has no spear.
Like his people, he holds touching the bodies of fallen kin to be deeply taboo.
He loves cards and bluffs superbly, thanks to his spy training and his people's restrained expressions.
He resents being treated as a symbol of his people or a curiosity, and hides his irritation at slights behind 'it's all right'. He wants to be seen simply as himself.
He wants to be valued for who he is, refusing a spren pushed into bonding him and rejoicing when one chose him freely.
